claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure containing an FCC-like phase and a B2-like phase.
The ordered brittle phase forms a continuous network interleaved with a softer, ductile phase in the starting eutectic alloy.
A solutionizing, rapid-quenching, and low-temperature-annealing sequence can invert phase connectivity, producing a continuous disordered matrix with discrete ordered precipitates.
The solutionizing step homogenizes the alloy and partially dissolves the brittle ordered phase.
Rapid quenching freezes in a metastable state that can subsequently be converted into the inverted microstructure by annealing.
Inverting phase connectivity reduces the extent of continuous internal boundaries that promote dislocation pile-ups.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups lowers local stress concentrations and the number of microcrack-initiation sites.
A continuous ductile matrix with discrete precipitates facilitates dislocation motion and produces more uniform plastic flow.
Discrete ordered precipitates provide load transfer and precipitation strengthening.
The proposed performance should be evaluated by room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing at a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The untreated eutectic alloy typically has only 10–15% room-temperature tensile elongation.
The untreated alloy fails in a brittle manner because its continuous brittle-phase network causes dislocation pile-ups and microcracking.
The treatment will increase tensile elongation from below approximately 12% to about 30–38% or higher.
The treated alloy will have a yield strength of approximately 1300–1350 MPa.
The treatment will maintain or slightly increase yield strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The improvement applies under room-temperature, quasi-static loading.
The outcome is sensitive to alloy composition, thermal history, and the precise heat-treatment parameters.
Residual grain coarsening or incomplete phase inversion may reduce the expected property improvements.

contradictions.description: The baseline states that the untreated eutectic alloy typically has 10–15% tensile ductility and brittle fracture, whereas the cited same-system AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy exhibited 25.6% room-temperature tensile elongation.
